title: Drumright, Oklahoma: the outlaw federal agents freed, and Officer Ulysses Lenox (1924)

sources.what: 'In 1920, he was sentenced to five years for automobile theft, but was paroled in 1922. He was arrested again on December 22, 1923, for a bank robbery in Grady County. However, in 1924, he was released to serve as an informant in the Osage Indian murders.' 'While Blackie did provide testimony against William King Hale and Ernest Burkhart, he quickly ran off and formed the "Thompson gang."' 'Thompson went on to kill police officer Ulysses Sterling Lenox in Drumright, Oklahoma on July 2, 1924, after robbing the First State Bank of Avery (2 other officers were injured).' 'Thompson was found guilty of murder and sentenced to life in prison.' Died December 6, 1934, Route 66, Amarillo, Texas; cause of death: gunshot wounds. 'Tommy Schultz portrayed Thompson in the 2023 film Killers of the Flower Moon.'
sources.who: Wikipedia, 'Blackie Thompson' (cites Laurence J. Yadon, 2008; Slate; Entertainment Weekly; Ardmore Daily Press, June 2, 1926)

sources.what: 'On the afternoon of Wednesday, July 2, 1924, a group of four officers from Drumright got in a car and drove off to intercept three men who had just robbed the State Bank of Avery, located seven miles south of Cushing. The bank robbers were headed northeast toward Drumright, which was seven miles away. About 2:15 p.m. a mile and a half southwest of Drumright the officer's and the bank robber's cars passed each other. As the two vehicles passed, the bank robbers opened fire on the officers' vehicle, wounding Drumright Chief of Police Jack Ary and Officer Ulysses Lenox. Creek Deputy Sheriff W. D. Norris was cut by flying glass and the fourth officer in the car, Constable A. F. Cline, was not injured. The bank robbers then sped off and escaped. Officer Ulysses Lenox died ten minutes after arriving at the hospital in Drumright.' 'Officer Ulysses Lenox, 38, left behind his wife Topse and their two young children.' 'Bank robbers Joe Clayton and Irvin "Blackie" Thompson were charged with Officer Ulysses Lenox's murder. Joe Clayton pled guilty to the murder and received a life sentence. Irvin "Blackie" Thompson was tried, found guilty and sentenced to life in prison.'
sources.who: Oklahoma Law Enforcement Memorial, 'Ulysses Sterling Lenox, Officer, Drumright Police Department, July 2, 1924'

sources.what: Full entry: Officer Lenox 'was shot and killed as he and three other officers searched for bank robbery suspects'; the four officers spotted the suspects' car and were turning around when the suspects opened fire; Officer Lenox and the Drumright police chief were wounded and a county deputy was hurt by flying glass; Lenox died within the hour. Age 38. Cause: gunfire. 'No one was ever arrested.' Offender: 'At large'.
sources.who: Officer Down Memorial Page, 'Police Officer Ulysses Sterling Lenox, Drumright Police Department, Oklahoma' (full entry on beta.odmp.org)

sources.what: William Weaver (real name Phoenix Donald) 'was also serving life, for the murder of Drumright, Oklahoma, Police Officer Ulysses S. Lenox, and the wounding of Drumright's Chief of Police, "Fighting Jack" Ary, in a gun battle that followed a bank robbery in Avery, Oklahoma, on July 2, 1924.'
sources.who: Tony Perrin, 'The Day the Barkers Brought Death to the Ozarks', RevolverGuy, Aug. 19, 2023

sources.what: 'In the 1920s, oil-rich Osage Indians in Oklahoma kept mysteriously dying. During a period that came to be called the "Reign of Terror," scores, perhaps hundreds, were murdered.' Quoting David Grann: 'The bureau badly bungled the case initially. They released an outlaw named Blackie Thompson, hoping he would work as an undercover informant, but he instead robbed banks and killed a police officer.'
sources.who: Christopher Klein, 'The FBI's First Big Case: The Osage Murders', History.com

sources.what: 'Agents released Blackie Thompson, a notorious outlaw, from jail, hoping to use him as an informant. Instead, he robbed a bank and killed a police officer. Thompson would later be gunned down himself.'
sources.who: PBS NewsHour, 'The forgotten murders of the Osage people for the oil beneath their land' (David Grann interview)

sources.what: Blackie Thompson: 'A notorious outlaw who is released from prison in order to go undercover and aid the bureau in gathering evidence on the Osage killings.'
sources.who: LitCharts, Killers of the Flower Moon by David Grann, character analysis

sources.what: 'Osage murders, series of murders of Osage tribal members in Oklahoma principally in the 1920s. Many of the killings were part of a conspiracy to obtain the oil wealth of Osage members.' '1921-26: the Reign of Terror.'

'As word spread, opportunists flocked to Osage lands seeking to separate the Osage from their wealth by any means necessary, even murder.' 'Newspapers described the murders and fear during this time as the Reign of Terror.' The Bureau of Investigation (the agency that would become the FBI) assigned agents after the Osage Tribal Council's petition in April 1923.
sources.who: FBI, History, Famous Cases: 'Osage Murders Case'

sources.what: Bureau agents 'released from prison a convicted bank robber named Blackie Thompson, who they hoped would help the investigation by working as an undercover informant.'
sources.who: Shortform summary of David Grann's Killers of the Flower Moon

sources.what: Special meeting at Huntsville, July 24, 1934, to investigate 'the matter of escape of Raymond Hamilton, Joe Palmer and Irvin (Blackie) Thompson, all three out of the death cell'; the three 'succeeded in getting over the walls at picket #7.'
sources.who: Texas Prison Board minutes, July 24, 1934 (Texas State Library and Archives Commission exhibit)

sources.what: 'Amarillo Cops Kill Blackie Thompson': Irvin Thompson, 'notorious bank robber and killer and escapee from the death house in the Texas penitentiary', 'was shot to death in a gun fight with Amarillo officers about 12 miles east of Amarillo last night'; he was 'one of three prisoners who escaped from the death house in the Texas penitentiary at Huntsville'.
sources.who: The Memphis Democrat (Memphis, Texas), Dec. 7, 1934, p. 1, via Texas Tech Southwest Collection

sourcing_note: Where the sources disagree the short leaves the detail out: the bank's name (Wikipedia 'First State Bank of Avery', the memorial 'State Bank of Avery': 'a bank in nearby Avery'); the year Thompson was let out (1924 Wikipedia, 1923 Shortform: no year); prison or jail ('let ... out'); how many others were hurt (only 'the police chief was wounded', which ODMP, the memorial and RevolverGuy all say); and whether anyone was ever convicted of the murder: the memorial says Joe Clayton pled guilty and Thompson was convicted and got life, Wikipedia says Thompson was found guilty, RevolverGuy says William Weaver was serving life for it, and ODMP's full entry says no one was ever arrested. So the short says nothing about an arrest or a conviction for Lenox's death, and never who fired. It ends with what is solid: Thompson kept robbing banks, escaped the Texas death house in July 1934 and was shot dead by Amarillo officers that December. 'As the cars passed' (the memorial) and 'tried to turn around' (ODMP) differ, so the picture shows only the two cars on the road and the robbers' car firing. The only time given (the memorial, about 2:15 p.m.) is afternoon, so beats 4-6 use a plain daytime sky.

beats.text: Federal agents freed an outlaw to help them catch killers. Instead, he became one. Drumright, Oklahoma, 1924.
beats.label: DRUMRIGHT, OKLAHOMA
beats.credit: History.com, on David Grann's book; Wikipedia; ODMP

beats.text: In the 1920s, Osage people were being murdered for their oil wealth. It came to be called the Reign of Terror.
beats.label: OSAGE COUNTY, OKLAHOMA
beats.credit: Britannica; History.com; FBI history: Osage Murders Case

beats.text: Agents let a bank robber named Blackie Thompson out, to work as their informant. He went back to robbing banks.
beats.label: THE INFORMANT
beats.credit: Wikipedia; History.com, on David Grann's book

beats.text: On July 2, 1924, a bank in nearby Avery was robbed. Word came the robbers were headed toward Drumright.
beats.label: AVERY, OKLAHOMA
beats.credit: Wikipedia; Oklahoma Law Enforcement Memorial; ODMP

beats.text: Four officers went after them, all in one car. Near Drumright, the robbers opened fire on them.
beats.credit: Officer Down Memorial Page; Oklahoma Law Enforcement Memorial

beats.text: The police chief was wounded. Officer Ulysses Lenox, 38, was killed.
beats.label: DRUMRIGHT POLICE
beats.credit: Oklahoma Law Enforcement Memorial; ODMP; RevolverGuy

beats.text: Blackie Thompson kept robbing banks. In 1934, he broke out of death row in Texas, and was gunned down himself.
beats.label: TEXAS, 1934
beats.credit: Wikipedia; Texas State Library; Memphis (Tex.) Democrat, 1934

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck: Independent check Nov. 15, 2026: beats 1-6 supported, but ODMP's full entry says 'No one was ever arrested' (offender 'At large'), against the memorial and Wikipedia (Thompson convicted, life) and RevolverGuy (William Weaver serving life): the conviction line was cut and beat 7 now says Thompson kept robbing banks, broke out of death row in Texas in 1934 and was gunned down himself (Texas Prison Board minutes, July 24, 1934; Memphis Democrat, Dec. 7, 1934; Wikipedia). 'Newspapers called it the Reign of Terror' became 'It came to be called the Reign of Terror' (Britannica, History.com). Lenox's age, 38, is now in two sources (ODMP and the memorial). Beats 4-6 got a daytime sky instead of the dusk-looking 'haze'. Credits fixed. Post text: 'four Drumright officers' became 'four officers' (a county deputy was in the car). No second check: the fixes follow the checker's sources, re-read Nov. 15.
